text: If $z\neq 0$ be a complex number such that $\left |z-\frac{1}{z}\right |=2$, then the maximum value of $|z|$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 29th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let $r=|z|>0$. Since $\left ||z|-\right |\dfrac{1}{z}\left |\right |\leq \left |z-\dfrac{1}{z}\right |=2$,

$\left |r-\dfrac{1}{r}\right |\leq 2$

From $r-\dfrac{1}{r}\leq 2$:

$r^{2}-2r-1\leq 0\Rightarrow r\leq 1+\sqrt{2}$

From $\dfrac{1}{r}-r\leq 2$:

$r^{2}+2r-1\geq 0\Rightarrow r\geq \sqrt{2}-1$

So $\sqrt{2}-1\leq |z|\leq \sqrt{2}+1$, where $\sqrt{2}-1$ is the least value, not the greatest.

For $z=1+\sqrt{2}$, $\dfrac{1}{z}=\sqrt{2}-1$ and $z-\dfrac{1}{z}=2$, so the upper bound is attained and the maximum value of $|z|$ is $\sqrt{2}+1$.

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 29th July Evening Shift

text: Which of the following matrices can NOT be obtained from the matrix $\left [\begin{array}{ll} -1 & 2 \\ 1 & -1 \end{array}\right ]$ by a single elementary row operation ?

solution.body:
Given matrix $A=\left [\begin{array}{ll} -1 & 2 \\ 1 & -1 \end{array}\right ]$

$R_{1}\to R_{1}+R_{2}$

$A=\left [\begin{array}{ll} 0 & 1 \\ 1 & -1 \end{array}\right ]$

$A=\left [\begin{array}{ll} 1 & -1 \\ -1 & 2 \end{array}\right ]$

$\therefore$ Option D can be obtained.

text:
If the system of equations

$\begin{array}{l} x+y+z=6 \\ 2x+5y+αz=β \\ x+2y+3z=14 \end{array}$

has infinitely many solutions, then $α+β$ is equal to
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 29th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given,

$x+y+z=6$ ...... (1)

$2x+5y+αz=β$ ..... (2)

$x+2y+3z=14$ ...... (3)

System of equation have infinite many solutions.

$\therefore$ $\Delta _{x}=\Delta _{y}=\Delta _{z}=0$ and $\Delta =0$

Now, $\Delta =\left |\begin{array}{lll} 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 2 & 5 & α \\ 1 & 2 & 3 \end{array}\right |=0$

$C_{1}\to C_{1}-C_{3}$

$C_{2}\to C_{2}-C_{3}$

$\Rightarrow \left |\begin{array}{lll} 0 & 0 & 1 \\ 2-α & 5-α & α \\ -2 & -1 & 3 \end{array}\right |=0$

$\Rightarrow -2+α+10-2α=0$

$\Rightarrow 8-α=0$

$\Rightarrow α=8$

Now, $x+y+z=6$

$2x+5y+8z=β$

$x+2y+3z=14$

$\therefore$ $\Delta _{x}=\left |\begin{array}{lll} 6 & 1 & 1 \\ β & 5 & 8 \\ 14 & 2 & 3 \end{array}\right |=0$

$C_{1}\to C_{1}-6C_{3}$

$C_{2}\to C_{2}-C_{3}$

$\Rightarrow \left |\begin{array}{lll} 0 & 0 & 1 \\ β-48 & -3 & 8 \\ -4 & -1 & 3 \end{array}\right |=0$

$\Rightarrow -β+48-12=0$

$\Rightarrow β=36$

$\therefore$ $α+β=8+36=44$

solution.body:

text: If $[t]$ denotes the greatest integer $\leq t$, then the value of $\int\limits _{0}^{1}\left [2x-\left |3x^{2}-5x+2\right |+1\right ]\mathrm{d}x$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 29th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Here $3x^{2}-5x+2=(3x-2)(x-1)$, which is non-negative on $\left [0,\dfrac{2}{3}\right ]$ and negative on $\left (\dfrac{2}{3},1\right )$.


[IMG]

So the integrand is $[f(x)]$ on $\left [0,\dfrac{2}{3}\right ]$ and $[g(x)]$ on $\left [\dfrac{2}{3},1\right ]$, where

$f(x)=2x-(3x^{2}-5x+2)+1=-3x^{2}+7x-1,g(x)=2x+(3x^{2}-5x+2)+1=3x^{2}-3x+3$

On $\left [0,\dfrac{2}{3}\right ]$, $f^{'}(x)=7-6x>0$, so $f$ increases from $f(0)=-1$ to $f\left (\dfrac{2}{3}\right )=\dfrac{7}{3}$ and crosses the integers $0,1,2$.

$f=0$: $3x^{2}-7x+1=0\Rightarrow x=\dfrac{7-\sqrt{37}}{6}$; $f=1$: $3x^{2}-7x+2=0\Rightarrow x=\dfrac{1}{3}$; $f=2$: $3x^{2}-7x+3=0\Rightarrow x=\dfrac{7-\sqrt{13}}{6}$. The other root of each equation exceeds $\dfrac{2}{3}$.

$\int\limits _{0}^{2/3}[f(x)]dx=(-1)\cdot \frac{7-\sqrt{37}}{6}+0+1\cdot \left (\frac{7-\sqrt{13}}{6}-\frac{1}{3}\right )+2\left (\frac{2}{3}-\frac{7-\sqrt{13}}{6}\right )=\frac{\sqrt{37}+\sqrt{13}-8}{6}$

On $\left [\dfrac{2}{3},1\right ]$, $g^{'}(x)=6x-3>0$, so $g$ increases from $g\left (\dfrac{2}{3}\right )=\dfrac{7}{3}$ to $g(1)=3$; thus $[g(x)]=2$ except at $x=1$.

$\int\limits _{2/3}^{1}[g(x)]dx=2\cdot \frac{1}{3}=\frac{4}{6}$

$\int\limits _{0}^{1}[\cdot ]dx=\frac{\sqrt{37}+\sqrt{13}-8}{6}+\frac{4}{6}=\frac{\sqrt{37}+\sqrt{13}-4}{6}$

Hence, the correct option is (A).

text: For $I(x)=\int \frac{\sec ^{2}x-2022}{\sin ^{2022}x}dx$, if $I\left (\frac{π}{4}\right )=2^{1011}$, then
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 29th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given,

$I(x)=\int \frac{\sec ^{2}x-2022}{\sin ^{2022}x}dx$

$=\int \frac{\sec ^{2}x}{\sin ^{2022}x}dx-\int \frac{2022}{\sin ^{2022}x}dx$

$=\int \frac{1}{\sin ^{2022}x}.\sec ^{2}xdx-\int \frac{2022}{\sin ^{2022}x}dx$

$=\frac{1}{\sin ^{2022}x}.\tan x-\int \left (\frac{-2022}{\sin ^{2023}x}.\cos x.\tan x\right )dx-\int \frac{2022}{\sin ^{2022}x}dx+C$

$=\frac{\tan x}{\sin ^{2022}x}+\int \left (\frac{2022}{\sin ^{2023}x}.\cos x.\frac{\sin x}{\cos x}\right )dx-\int \frac{2022}{\sin ^{2022}x}dx+C$

$=\frac{\tan x}{\sin ^{2022}x}+\int \frac{2022}{\sin ^{2022}x}dx-\int \frac{2022}{\sin ^{2022}x}dx$

$=\frac{\tan x}{\sin ^{2022}x}+C$

Given, $I\left (\frac{π}{4}\right )=2^{1011}$

$\therefore$ $I\left (\frac{π}{4}\right )=\frac{\tan \left (\frac{π}{4}\right )}{\left (\sin \frac{π}{4}\right )^{2022}}+C$

$\Rightarrow 2^{1011}=\frac{1}{\left (\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right )^{2022}}+C$

$\Rightarrow C=2^{1011}-2^{1011}=0$

$\therefore$ $I(x)=\frac{\tan x}{\sin ^{2022}x}$

$\therefore$ $I\left (\frac{π}{3}\right )=\frac{\tan \frac{π}{3}}{\left (\sin \frac{π}{3}\right )^{2022}}=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{\left (\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right )^{2022}}$

$I\left (\frac{π}{6}\right )=\frac{\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}}{\left (\frac{1}{2}\right )^{2022}}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\times (2)^{2022}$

From option (A),

$3^{1010}\qquad .I\left (\frac{π}{3}\right )-I\left (\frac{π}{6}\right )$

$=3^{1010}.\sqrt{3}.\left (\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}\right )^{2022}-\frac{(2)^{2022}}{\sqrt{3}}$

$=3^{1010}.\sqrt{3}\times \frac{2^{2022}}{3^{1011}}-\frac{2^{2022}}{\sqrt{3}}$

$=\frac{2^{2022}}{\sqrt{3}}-\frac{2^{2022}}{\sqrt{3}}=0$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 29th July Evening Shift

text: If the solution curve of the differential equation $\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{x+y-2}{x-y}$ passes through the points $(2,1)$ and $(\mathrm{k}+1,2),\mathrm{k}>0$, then
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 29th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{x+y-2}{x-y}=\frac{(x-1)+(y-1)}{(x-1)-(y-1)}$

Let $x-1=X,y-1=Y$

$\frac{dY}{dX}=\frac{X+Y}{X-Y}$

Let $Y=tX\Rightarrow \frac{dY}{dX}=t+X\frac{dt}{dX}$

$t+X\frac{dt}{dX}=\frac{1+t}{1-t}$

$X\frac{dt}{dX}=\frac{1+t}{1-t}-t=\frac{1+t^{2}}{1-t}$

$\int \frac{1-t}{1+t^{2}}dt=\int \frac{dX}{X}$

$\begin{array}{l} \tan ^{-1}t-\dfrac{1}{2}\ln \left (1+t^{2}\right )=\ln |X|+c \\  \\ \tan ^{-1}\left (\dfrac{y-1}{x-1}\right )-\dfrac{1}{2}\ln \left (1+\left (\dfrac{y-1}{x-1}\right )^{2}\right )=\ln |x-1|+c \end{array}$

Curve passes through $(2,1)$

$0-0=0+c\Rightarrow c=0$

If $(k+1,2)$ also satisfies the curve

$\begin{array}{l} \tan ^{-1}\left (\dfrac{1}{k}\right )-\dfrac{1}{2}\ln \left (\dfrac{1+k^{2}}{k^{2}}\right )=\ln k \\  \\ 2\tan ^{-1}\left (\dfrac{1}{k}\right )=\ln \left (1+k^{2}\right ) \end{array}$

text: Let $y=y(x)$ be the solution curve of the differential equation $\frac{dy}{dx}+\left (\frac{2x^{2}+11x+13}{x^{3}+6x^{2}+11x+6}\right )y=\frac{(x+3)}{x+1},x>-1$, which passes through the point $(0,1)$. Then $y(1)$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 29th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\frac{dy}{dx}+\left (\frac{2x^{2}+11x+13}{x^{3}+6x^{2}+11x+6}\right )y=\frac{(x+3)}{x+1},x>-1$,

Integrating factor I.F. $=e^{\int \frac{2x2+11x+13}{x3+6x2+11x+6}dx}$

$\begin{array}{l} \text{Let}\dfrac{2x^{2}+11x+13}{(x+1)(x+2)(x+3)}=\dfrac{A}{x+1}+\dfrac{B}{x+2}+\dfrac{C}{x+3} \\  \\ A=2,B=1,C=-1 \\  \\ \text{I.F.}=e^{(2\ln |x+1|+\ln |x+2|-\ln |x+3|)} \\  \\ =\dfrac{(x+1)^{2}(x+2)}{x+3} \end{array}$

Solution of differential equation

$\begin{array}{l} y\cdot \dfrac{(x+1)^{2}(x+2)}{x+3}=\int (x+1)(x+2)dx \\  \\ y\dfrac{(x+1)^{2}(x+2)}{x+3}=\dfrac{x^{3}}{3}+\dfrac{3x^{2}}{2}+2x+c \end{array}$

Curve passes through $(0,1)$

$\begin{array}{l} 1\times \dfrac{1\times 2}{3}=0+c\Rightarrow c=\dfrac{2}{3} \\  \\ \text{So,}y(1)=\dfrac{\frac{1}{3}+\frac{3}{2}+2+\frac{2}{3}}{\frac{(2^{2}\times 3)}{4}}=\dfrac{3}{2} \end{array}$

text: Let $m_{1},m_{2}$ be the slopes of two adjacent sides of a square of side a such that $a^{2}+11a+3\left (m_{1}^{2}+m_{2}^{2}\right )=220$. If one vertex of the square is $(10(\cos α-\sin α),10(\sin α+\cos α))$, where $α\in \left (0,\frac{π}{2}\right )$ and the equation of one diagonal is $(\cos α-\sin α)x+(\sin α+\cos α)y=10$, then $72\left (\sin ^{4}α+\cos ^{4}α\right )+a^{2}-3a+13$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 29th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)
tags: straight lines and pair of straight lines

solution.body:
Write $c=\cos α$, $s=\sin α$. For the vertex $P(10(c-s),10(s+c))$, $(c-s)\cdot 10(c-s)+(s+c)\cdot 10(s+c)=20\neq 10$, so $P$ is not on the diagonal $(c-s)x+(s+c)y=10$; this line is the other diagonal.

The diagonal through $P$ is perpendicular to it, so it runs along the normal $(c-s,s+c)$. Since $P=10(c-s,s+c)$, this diagonal passes through the origin $O$.

The diagonals meet at the foot of the perpendicular from $O$ to $(c-s)x+(s+c)y=10$, which is $k(c-s,s+c)$ with $2k=10$, i.e. $(5(c-s),5(s+c))$, the midpoint of $OP$. So the vertex opposite $P$ is $O$.

$OP=10\sqrt{(c-s)^{2}+(s+c)^{2}}=10\sqrt{2}\Rightarrow a=\frac{OP}{\sqrt{2}}=10$

Then $100+110+3(m_{1}^{2}+m_{2}^{2})=220$, so $m_{1}^{2}+m_{2}^{2}=\dfrac{10}{3}$. Adjacent sides are perpendicular, so $m_{1}m_{2}=-1$:

$m_{1}^{2}+\frac{1}{m_{1}^{2}}=\frac{10}{3}\Rightarrow m_{1}^{2}=3\text{or}\frac{1}{3}$

The diagonal $OP$ has direction $(c-s,s+c)=\sqrt{2}\left (\cos \left (α+\dfrac{π}{4}\right ),\sin \left (α+\dfrac{π}{4}\right )\right )$. The sides through $O$ make $\dfrac{π}{4}$ with it, so they are inclined at $α$ and $α+\dfrac{π}{2}$, with slopes $\tan α$ and $-\cot α$. Hence $\tan ^{2}α=3$ or $\dfrac{1}{3}$, and in both cases

$\sin ^{2}2α=\frac{4\tan ^{2}α}{(1+\tan ^{2}α)^{2}}=\frac{3}{4}$

$\sin ^{4}α+\cos ^{4}α=1-\frac{1}{2}\sin ^{2}2α=1-\frac{3}{8}=\frac{5}{8}$

$72\cdot \frac{5}{8}+a^{2}-3a+13=45+100-30+13=128$

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 29th July Evening Shift

sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 29th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let $E\to$ Ball drawn from Bag II is black.

$E_{R}\to$ Bag I to Bag II red ball transferred.

$E_{B}\to$ Bag I to Bag II black ball transferred.

$E_{w}\to$ Bag I to Bag II white ball transferred.

$P(E_{R}/E)=\frac{P(E/E_{R})\cdot P(E_{R})}{P(E/E_{R})P(E_{R})+P(E/E_{B})P(E_{B})+P(E/E_{W})P(E_{W})}$

Here,

$P(E_{R})=3/10,P(E_{B})=4/10,P(E_{W})=3/10$

and

$\begin{array}{l} P(E/E_{R})=5/10,P(E/E_{B})=6/10,P(E/E_{W})=5/10 \\  \\ \therefore \quad P(E_{R}/E)=\dfrac{15/100}{15/100+24/100+15/100} \\  \\ =\dfrac{15}{54}=\dfrac{5}{18} \end{array}$

text: Let $X=\left [\begin{array}{l} 1 \\ 1 \\ 1 \end{array}\right ]$ and $A=\left [\begin{array}{lll} -1 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & 6 \\ 0 & 0 & -1 \end{array}\right ]$. For $\mathrm{k}\in N$, if $X^{'}A^{k}X=33$, then $\mathrm{k}$ is equal to $_______$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 29th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given $A=\left [\begin{array}{lll} -1 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & 6 \\ 0 & 0 & -1 \end{array}\right ]$

$A^{2}=\left [\begin{array}{lll} 1 & 0 & 6 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \end{array}\right ],A^{4}=\left [\begin{array}{lll} 1 & 0 & 12 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \end{array}\right ]$

$\Rightarrow A^{k}=\left [\begin{array}{lll} 1 & 0 & 3k \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \end{array}\right ]$

$\therefore X^{'}A^{k}X=[1 1 1]\left [\begin{array}{lll} 1 & 0 & 3k \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \end{array}\right ]\left [\begin{array}{l} 1 \\ 1 \\ 1 \end{array}\right ]=[3k+3]$

$\Rightarrow [3k+3]=33$ (here it shall be [33] as matrix can't be equal to a scalar)

i.e. $[3k+3]=33$

$3k+3=[33]\Rightarrow k=10$

If $k$ is odd and apply above process, we don't get odd value of $k$

$\therefore k=10$

text: If $[t]$ denotes the greatest integer $\leq t$, then the number of points, at which the function $f(x)=4|2x+3|+9\left [x+\frac{1}{2}\right ]-12[x+20]$ is not differentiable in the open interval $(-20,20)$, is $__________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 29th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$f(x)=4|2x+3|+9\left [x+\frac{1}{2}\right ]-12[x+20]$

$=4|2x+3|+9\left [x+\frac{1}{2}\right ]-12[x]-240$

$f(x)$ is non differentiable at $x=-\frac{3}{2}$

and $f(x)$ is discontinuous at $\{-19,-18,\ldots .,18,19\}$ 

as well as $\left \{-\frac{39}{2},-\frac{37}{2},\ldots ,-\frac{3}{2},-\frac{1}{2},\frac{1}{2},\ldots ,\frac{39}{2}\right \}$, 

at same point they are also non differentiable

$\begin{array}{ll} \therefore  & \text{Total number of points of non differentiability} \\ =39+40 \\ =79 \end{array}$

text:
Let $S=\left \{(x,y)\in \mathrm{ℕ}\times \mathrm{ℕ}:9(x-3)^{2}+16(y-4)^{2}\leq 144\right \}$ and
$T=\left \{(x,y)\in \mathrm{ℝ}\times \mathrm{ℝ}:(x-7)^{2}+(y-4)^{2}\leq 36\right \}$. Then $n(S\cap T)$ is equal to $__________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 29th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$S$ is the set of points with natural coordinates on or inside the ellipse $\dfrac{(x-3)^{2}}{16}+\dfrac{(y-4)^{2}}{9}\leq 1$, so $1\leq x\leq 7$ and $1\leq y\leq 7$. Column by column, $16(y-4)^{2}\leq 144-9(x-3)^{2}$ gives:

$x=3$: $(y-4)^{2}\leq 9$, $y=1,\ldots ,7$: 7 points.

$x=2,4$: $(y-4)^{2}\leq \dfrac{135}{16}$, $y=2,\ldots ,6$: 5 points each.

$x=1,5$: $(y-4)^{2}\leq \dfrac{108}{16}$, $y=2,\ldots ,6$: 5 points each.

$x=6$: $(y-4)^{2}\leq \dfrac{63}{16}$, $y=3,4,5$: 3 points.

$x=7$: $(y-4)^{2}\leq 0$, $y=4$: 1 point.

So $n(S)=7+10+10+3+1=31$.

$T$ is the disc $(x-7)^{2}+(y-4)^{2}\leq 36$. For every point of $S$ with $2\leq x\leq 7$, $(x-7)^{2}\leq 25$ and $(y-4)^{2}\leq 9$, so the sum is at most $34\leq 36$ and the point lies in $T$.

For $x=1$, $(x-7)^{2}=36$, so only $y=4$ is allowed; the points $(1,2),(1,3),(1,5),(1,6)$ are excluded.

$n(S\cap T)=31-4=27$

Hence, the answer is 27.
